arxiv-1505-02833.title: Bispectrality of 𝑵 \boldsymbol{N} -Component KP Wave Functions: A Study in Non-Commutativity
arxiv-1505-02833.creator: Alex KASMAN
arxiv-1505-02833.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Alex KASMAN. A wave function of the N N -component KP Hierarchy with continuous flows determined by an invertible matrix H H is constructed from the choice of an M ​ N MN -dimensional space of finitely-supported vector distributions. This wave function is shown to be an eigenfunction for a ring of matrix differential operators in x x having eigenvalues that are matrix functions of the spectral parameter z z .

arxiv-2104-07496.title: Unmasking the Mask – Evaluating Social Biases in Masked Language Models
arxiv-2104-07496.creator: Masahiro Kaneko, Danushka Bollegala
arxiv-2104-07496.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Masahiro Kaneko, Danushka Bollegala. Masked Language Models (MLMs) have shown superior performances in numerous downstream NLP tasks when used as text encoders. Unfortunately, MLMs also demonstrate significantly worrying levels of social biases. We show that the previously proposed evaluation metrics for quantifying the social biases in MLMs are problematic due to following reasons: (1) prediction accuracy of the masked tokens itself tend to be low in some MLMs, which raises questions regarding the reliability of the evaluation metrics that use the (pseudo) likelihood of

arxiv-2207-09195.title: Two-dimensional solitons in nonlocal media: a brief review
arxiv-2207-09195.creator: Boris A. Malomed 1,2
arxiv-2207-09195.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Boris A. Malomed 1,2. This is a review addressing soliton-like states in systems with nonlocal nonlinearity. The work on this topic has long history in optics and related areas. Some results produced by the work (such as solitons supported by thermal nonlinearity in optical glasses, and orientational nonlinearity which affects light propagation in liquid crystals) are well known, and have been properly reviewed in the literature, therefore the respective models are outlined in the present review in a brief form.

arxiv-2207-10786.title: Delayed Feedback in Generalised Linear Bandits Revisited
arxiv-2207-10786.creator: Benjamin Howson, Ciara Pike-Burke, Sarah Filippi
arxiv-2207-10786.description: Abstract The stochastic generalised linear bandit is a well-understood model for sequential decision-making problems, with many algorithms achieving near-optimal regret guarantees under immediate feedback. However, the stringent requirement for immediate rewards is unmet in many real-world applications where the reward is almost always delayed. We study the phenomenon of delayed rewards in generalised linear bandits in a theoretical manner.

arxiv-2307-12868.title: Understanding the Latent Space of Diffusion Models through the Lens of Riemannian Geometry
arxiv-2307-12868.creator: Yong-Hyun Park, Mingi Kwon, Jaewoong Choi, Junghyo Jo, Youngjung Uh
arxiv-2307-12868.description: Abstract Despite the success of diffusion models (DMs), we still lack a thorough understanding of their latent space. To understand the latent space 𝐱 t ∈ 𝒳 \mathbf{x}_{t}\in\mathcal{X} , we analyze them from a geometrical perspective. Our approach involves deriving the local latent basis within 𝒳 \mathcal{X} by leveraging the pullback metric associated with their encoding feature maps.

arxiv-2309-02917.title: GroupEnc : encoder with group loss for global structure preservation
arxiv-2309-02917.creator: David Novak, Sofie Van Gassen, Yvan Saeys
arxiv-2309-02917.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David Novak, Sofie Van Gassen, Yvan Saeys. Recent advances in dimensionality reduction have achieved more accurate lower-dimensional embeddings of high-dimensional data. In addition to visualisation purposes, these embeddings can be used for downstream processing, including batch effect normalisation, clustering, community detection or trajectory inference. We use the notion of structure preservation at both local and global levels to create a deep learning model, based on a variational autoencoder (VAE) and the stochastic quartet loss from the SQuadMDS algorithm.

arxiv-2411-05967.title: Locales as spaces in outer models
arxiv-2411-05967.creator: Nathaniel Bannister Carnegie Mellon University
arxiv-2411-05967.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nathaniel Bannister Carnegie Mellon University. Let M be a transitive model of set theory and X be a space in the sense of M. Is there a reasonable way to interpret X as a space in V? A general theory due to Zapletal ( [ 8 ] ) provides a natural candidate which behaves well on sufficiently complete spaces (for instance Čech complete spaces) but behaves poorly on more general spaces - for instance, the Zapletal interpretation does not commute with products.

arxiv-2510-04814.title: Robust stability of event-triggered nonlinear moving horizon estimation
arxiv-2510-04814.creator: Isabelle Krauss, Victor G. Lopez, Matthias A. Müller
arxiv-2510-04814.description: Abstract Zusammenfassung In this work, we propose an event-triggered moving horizon estimation (ET-MHE) scheme for the remote state estimation of general nonlinear systems. In the presented method, whenever an event is triggered, a single measurement is transmitted and the nonlinear MHE optimization problem is subsequently solved.

pmc-10634022.creator: Soohyun Park, Myeongsu Na, Sunghoe Chang, Ki Hean Kim
pmc-10634022.description: BackgroundOpen-top light-sheet microscopy (OT-LSM) is a specialized microscopic technique for the high-throughput cellular imaging of optically cleared, large-sized specimens, such as the brain. Despite the development of various OT-LSM techniques, achieving submicron resolution in all dimensions remains.ResultsWe developed a high-resolution open-top axially swept LSM (HR-OTAS-LSM) for high-throughput and high-resolution imaging in all dimensions.

pmc-10695100.description: Purpose:Preclinical studies show that activation of AMP kinase by phenformin can augment the cytotoxic effect and RAF inhibitors in BRAF V600-mutated melanoma. We conducted a phase Ib dose-escalation trial of phenformin with standard dose dabrafenib/trametinib in patients with metastatic BRAF V600-mutated melanoma.Experimental Design:We used a 3+3 dose-escalation design which explored phenformin doses between 50 and 200 mg twice daily.

pmc-11678625.title: Ischemic Stroke in Women: Understanding Sex-Specific Risk Factors, Treatment Considerations, and Outcomes
pmc-11678625.creator: Pei Chia Eng, Lyeann Li Ying Tan, Tamara N Kimball, Savvina Prapiadou, Benjamin Y Q Tan, Peter Kokkinos
pmc-11678625.description: Ischemic stroke is a major cause of mortality and disability and has become a significant public health concern among women. Overall, women have more ischemic stroke events than men, in part due to their longer life span, and also suffer from more severe stroke-related disabilities compared to men.

pmc-12394454.title: DARTS: Multi-year database of AI-detected retrogressive thaw slumps in the circum-arctic permafrost region
pmc-12394454.creator: Ingmar Nitze, Konrad Heidler, Nina Nesterova, Jonas Küpper, Emma Schütt, Tobias Hölzer, Sophia Barth, Mark J. Lara, Anna K. Liljedahl, Guido Grosse
pmc-12394454.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Retrogressive Thaw Slumps (RTS) are widespread mass-wasting hillslope failures triggered by thawing permafrost. While regional studies have provided insights into the spatial distribution and dynamics of RTS, a consistent and unbiased quantification and monitoring remains unsolved at pan-arctic scales. We present the Database of AI-detected Arctic RTS footprints (DARTS), comprising ~43,000 individual footprints of active RTS or active areas within larger RTS landforms. DARTS spans ~1.6 million km2 from 2018–2023, with at least annual coverage from 2021–2023 across a ~900,000 km2 region.

pmc-12507904.title: Prevalence of post COVID-19 condition and associations with risk factors among U.S. adults: 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System
pmc-12507904.creator: Gregory W. Heath, David Levine, Gloria Oppong, Majdi Alghader
pmc-12507904.description: IntroductionDuring the COVID-19 pandemic, between 12 and 20% of US adults were identified as having post-COVID-19 condition, commonly referred to as ‘Long COVID’. These individuals maintained symptoms of COVID-19 for 3 months or longer following their illness but lacked an active infection.

pmc-12872855.title: Multi-omics integration and machine learning-driven construction of an immunogenic cell death prognostic model for colon cancer and functional validation of FCGR2A
pmc-12872855.creator: Haipeng Wang, Ningning Chen, Weijia Wang
pmc-12872855.description: BackgroundImmunogenic cell death (ICD) influences tumor immune microenvironment remodeling and immunotherapy response. However, the prognostic value of ICD-related genes in colon cancer has not been systematically clarified. This study aimed to develop an ICD-based prognostic model and explore its association with the immune microenvironment and treatment sensitivity.

pmc-13043304.title: Bridging heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysis in carbon dioxide valorization
pmc-13043304.creator: Sergio Posada-Pérez, Anna Vidal-López, Aleix Comas-Vives, Albert Poater
pmc-13043304.description: The valorization of carbon dioxide (CO2) into fuels and chemicals represents both a scientific challenge and an opportunity for sustainable energy transition. This review bridges heterogeneous and homogeneous approaches, highlighting how molecular precision and materials robustness can converge to address the intrinsic stability of CO2 and the complexity of its multi-electron transformations.

pmc-13069678.title: T-ChroNet: Time-aware chromatin network reconstruction to detect dynamic regulatory programs in longitudinal epigenetic dataset
pmc-13069678.creator: Stefano Di Giovenale, Ottavio Lischio, Clelia Cortile, Giacomo Corleone, Maurizio Fanciulli, Francesco Bonchi, Iros Barozzi
pmc-13069678.description: Networks are widely applied to investigate relationships among individual components of complex biological systems. Recent application of biological networks, such as gene co-expression networks and gene regulatory networks, has been instrumental to define principles of transcriptional modulation in development and disease. However, computational methods that can embed the activity of cis-regulatory elements (CRE) into a network are still limited.

pmc-13340371.title: Direct to consumer genetic testing and gamete donor conception: ethical challenges
pmc-13340371.creator: Lucy Frith
pmc-13340371.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This paper examines recent developments in direct-to-consumer genetic (DNA) testing (DTCGT) and the ethical challenges it raises for those affected by donor conception (using donated gametes, eggs and sperm, to conceive children). First, DTCGT can result in the complete removal of donor anonymity at any stage in the donor conceived person’s life, and this has widespread implications for all those involved in donor conception. Second, for regulators: DTCGT can disrupt regulatory prohibitions on information disclosure.

pmc-13396769.title: Non-coding structural variants disrupt FOXG1 transcriptional regulation in early neurodevelopment
pmc-13396769.creator: Lisa Hamerlinck, Eva D’haene, Michael B Vaughan, Nore Van Loon, María del Rocío Pérez Baca, Sebastian Leimbacher, Michael Kosicki, Lara Colombo, Lukas Genbrugge, Lies Vantomme, Esperanza Daal, Luiza Lorena Pires Ramos, Daniela Mircheva Avdjieva-Tzavella, Himanshu Goel, Koen Devriendt, Albena Jordano
pmc-13396769.description: The FOXG1 transcription factor is a crucial regulator of embryonic brain development. Pathogenic FOXG1 variants cause FOXG1 syndrome. Although structural variants in the non-coding region downstream of FOXG1 have been reported in 38 individuals with similar characteristics, the regulatory pathomechanisms remain unknown.

pmc-13469292.title: The epidemiology and disease burden of enterovirus infections among hospitalized children in China: An 8-year national cross-sectional study
pmc-13469292.creator: Yi Wang, Fei Li, Hui Xu, Yiliang Fu, Guoshuang Feng, Hanwen Zhang, Juan Huang, Zhengde Xie, Xiangpeng Chen
pmc-13469292.description: Enterovirus (EV) infections represent a significant global and national health concern in children, leading to various complications. Although most children with EV infections generally have a favorable prognosis, a small proportion may still develop severe complications. This study aimed to analyze the epidemiological characteristics, disease spectrum, and disease burden of EV infections in China.

pmc-13597346.title: First-trimester SPISE mediates the association between early-pregnancy body fat percentage change and gestational diabetes mellitus: an exploratory secondary analysis of a prospective cohort
pmc-13597346.creator: Xuran Zhang, Meiyuan Guo, Yingjie Chen
pmc-13597346.description: BackgroundGestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is closely related to maternal adiposity and insulin resistance. The rate of body fat percentage (BFP) change in early pregnancy may describe estimated BFP gain before routine glucose screening. The Single-Point Insulin Sensitivity Estimator (SPISE) offers a fasting estimate of insulin sensitivity without insulin testing.

pmc-13662736.title: Doggy doctorates: Early career progression outcomes for UK‐funded postgraduate canine health and welfare researchers
pmc-13662736.creator: Alison M Skipper, Rowena M A Packer, Dan G O'Neill
pmc-13662736.description: BackgroundThis quantitative study describes characteristics and career outcomes (in August 2024) of students completing research master's or PhD degrees in canine health and welfare who received not‐for‐profit funding between 2012 and 2018.MethodsHistorical canine health and welfare research funding data were used to identify research students whose subsequent career outcomes were established by visual scrutiny of public online databases.
